skills-reading-s1.title: Total population of South Asian countries

map.label: Shaded map of South Asia by total population: India is in the darkest class, Pakistan and Bangladesh in the next, Afghanistan, Nepal and Sri Lanka in the third, and Bhutan in the lightest

skills-reading-s2.title: People living in two towns, 1990 to 2020

plot.label: Line chart of two invented towns: River Town grows from 20,000 to 50,000 people between 1990 and 2020, while Hill Town falls from 30,000 to 22,000

items.q: Read the legend of this map. What do the shades measure?
options: The total number of people in each country
How many people live in each square kilometer
How fast each country's population is growing
The share of each country's people who live in cities

why.correct: The legend title and the classes (millions, a billion) show a total: the number of people in each country.
options: Right: the legend title is "Total population (number of people)", and the classes are counts of people.
That would be people per unit of land, a rate. The legend counts people and says nothing about land area.
Growth needs numbers from two dates. This map shows one count, from 2024.
A share is a percent. The classes here are counts in millions and billions, not percents.

items.q: Which statement describes the pattern on this map, naming places?
options: Bangladesh is in the top class and India in the second class
India is in the top class (1 billion or more) and Bhutan in the lowest (under 10 million)
Afghanistan and Nepal are in the darkest class, and India is in the lightest class
Sri Lanka and Pakistan are both in the lowest class

why.correct: A good pattern statement names the places and the values: India at 1 billion or more, Bhutan under 10 million.
options: Read the shades again: India is the darkest; Bangladesh is one class lower, with Pakistan.
Right: it names places, their classes and the values of those classes.
The map has four classes in use, from Bhutan (lightest) to India (darkest).
Sri Lanka is in the 10 to 99 million class and Pakistan in the 100 to 999 million class; Bhutan is the lightest.

items.q: A student looks at this map and writes: "India is the most crowded country in South Asia, because it is the darkest." What is wrong with the claim?
options: The map has no source line, so a reader has no way to check where its numbers came from
Dark shades on this map stand for the lowest values, so India has the fewest people shown
It reads a totals map as a crowding map; Bangladesh fits more people on each square kilometer
India is shaded in the lightest class, so the student read the colors in reverse

why.correct: Totals on a shaded map favor big countries. To judge crowding you need people per unit of land, which this map does not show.
options: The map does have a source line: UN World Population Prospects 2024.
The legend runs from light (under 10 million) to dark (1 billion or more), so dark means high.
Right: a total says nothing about how much land the people share. Bangladesh is small and very crowded (UN WPP 2024), yet it is a class lighter than India.
India is marked on the map and shaded in the darkest class.

items.q: What trend does the chart show for River Town?
options: It shrank in each decade, from about 50,000 people in 1990 to about 20,000 in 2020
It stayed at about 30,000 people from 1990 to 2020, with little change
It grew until 2000 and then shrank in each decade after that
It grew each decade, from about 20,000 people in 1990 to about 50,000 in 2020

why.correct: River Town's line rises from 20 to 50 (thousands of people): a rising trend over 30 years.
options: Read the years along the bottom: 1990 is on the left, so the line rises over time.
That is close to Hill Town's 1990 value, not River Town's line.
River Town's line rises in each decade; it is Hill Town that falls after 1990.
Right: a trend gives the direction, the dates and the size of the change.

items.q: In which year did the two towns have about the same number of people?

why.correct: The lines cross near 2000, where both towns had about 28,000 people.
options: Right: both lines are at about 28 (thousand) in 2000.
In 1990 Hill Town had about 30,000 people and River Town about 20,000.
By 2010 River Town (about 38,000) had passed Hill Town (about 25,000).
In 2020 the gap was widest: about 50,000 against about 22,000.

items.q: Which statement can you support with this chart, and which needs other data?
options: Supported: people moved from Hill Town to River Town. Needs other data: the years
Supported: Hill Town lost people from 1990 to 2020. Needs other data: why people left
Supported: River Town has more jobs. Needs other data: the number of people
Supported: both towns grew over the 30 years. Needs other data: the units on the axis

why.correct: A chart shows what changed and when. Why it changed is a claim that needs more evidence.
options: The chart never shows people moving between the towns; one town may have grown for other reasons.
Right: the chart shows how many people, not why. A reason needs another source, such as interviews or job data.
Jobs are not on the chart at all, while the number of people is.
Hill Town shrank, and the units (thousands of people) are on the axis.

items.q: Which source line is complete enough to trust for a class report?
options: From the internet, found by searching for the topic
A website about countries, with facts about each one
UN World Population Prospects 2024, 2024 estimates
Government numbers, recent, from the population office

why.correct: A useful source line names who made the data and when. Without a year you cannot tell how out of date a number is.
options: It names no maker and no year, so you cannot check it or know how old it is.
A website is not a named source, and there is no year.
Right: it names who made the data and the year of the data.
"Recent" is not a year. Numbers like these change, so a year matters.

items.q: In an invented town of 40,000 people, 10,000 people ride a bus each day. What percent of the town's people ride a bus each day?

mistakes.why: You divided the whole by the part. A share is the part (riders) divided by the whole (all the people), times 100.

items.q: A table lists "Hospital beds per 1,000 people": Town P has 4 and Town Q has 2. Which statement does the table support?
options: Town P has more hospital beds in total than Town Q
Town Q has more people than Town P
Town Q has 2 hospital beds, half as many as Town P has
Town P has more beds for each 1,000 people than Town Q

why.correct: Read the unit in the header. "Per 1,000 people" is a rate, so it compares how well each town is served, not how many beds each has.
options: A rate does not give a total. If Town Q has many more people, it could have as many beds or more.
The table gives no populations, so you cannot tell which town is bigger.
The 2 is a rate, 2 beds for each 1,000 people, not a count of beds.
Right: the unit is a rate, beds for each 1,000 people, and 4 is more than 2.

items.q: Put the four steps for reading a map, table or chart in order.
options: Read the title: what, where and when
Read the legend and the units
Read the source line: who and what year
Describe the pattern, naming places and values

why.correct: Start with what the figure is about, learn what its marks and units mean, check where the data came from, and only then describe the pattern.
